featureName: BUG-104-001: smackerel_self namespace race between integration test packages

executionHistory.note: Added tests/integration/nslock session-level advisory lock plus exclusion and key-derivation guards. Full integration suite exits 0 (1969 PASS, 0 FAIL).

7 findings. F2 (unlocked TRUNCATE artifacts in a THIRD package), F3 (unlocked e2e inserts), F5 (guards proved the mechanism, not the call sites) and F6 (two comments stating incorrect release/scope semantics) remediated. F4 (production stale sweeper wipes test rows on core restart) recorded as unresolved. Independently re-ran the suite: INTEGRATION_EXIT=0.

A1 CRITICAL overturned the root-cause diagnosis: go-integration.sh passes -p 1, so the two packages never run concurrently and the documented interleaving is unreachable. A2/A3/A4 showed the call-site guard missed 2 of the 3 originally-failing tests (helper-built SQL) and was held for two others only by comment text. Guard rewritten with a named floor plus discovery; both probes verified. Artifacts corrected to state the lock is defence-in-depth and F4 is the primary hypothesis.

SCOPE-01.name: Mutual exclusion for the shared smackerel_self namespace

certification.basis: NOT certified. The hardening is complete, guarded and green (three consecutive full integration runs at exit 0), but audit finding A1 established that the documented root-cause mechanism is unreachable under `-p 1`, so the original failure is NOT root-caused. Closing this as done would record a fix for a mechanism that cannot fire while the one that can (F4, the production boot-time stale sweeper) is unaddressed.

notes: Pre-existing defect, not introduced by this session's commits.

A1 (audit): scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh passes `-p 1`; no contending file calls t.Parallel(); the go/python lanes are sequential docker runs. The two packages never run concurrently, so the documented interleaving was unreachable during the original red.
The landed lock is DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH: it makes exclusion a property of the namespace rather than of a flag in a shell script, and covers a future `-p >1` or a shared-DB cross-lane run.

F4 is the primary remaining hypothesis: internal/assistant/selfknowledge/ingestor.go deletes every smackerel_self row whose content_hash is absent from the corpus, which is every row these tests insert. It runs at core boot, and the core container is not serialised by -p 1.
The production stale sweep itself is designed behaviour and is unchanged.
